text:
asha: quick check for SDK folks: saw User-Agent 'Redwood-Go/0.3.1 go1.20' in logs. Is that the intended stable UA for the Go client?
jon: yes, Go client sets User-Agent to `Redwood-Go/<pkg-ver> go/<runtime-ver>` so infra can roll up by client lang + version. We also append a short build token in CI builds unless telemetry is disabled.
sam: FYI browsers can't set the standard User-Agent header from JS, so for browser/edge bundles we emit `Redwood-Client/<pkg-ver> web` server-side and expose a permissable header `x-rw-client` for apps to add details.
maria: How should teams opt out of client-side telemetry & UA tokens? Need both code and env examples for docs.
devops-bot: In hosted/dedicated setups telemetry is ON by default. Private installs default OFF. Env toggles we support: `REDWOOD_SDK_DISABLE_TELEMETRY=true` (legacy) and `REDWOOD_CLIENT_TELEMETRY=false`. Client option takes precedence.
jon: code examples:
Node (override UA and disable telemetry):
```js
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY, headers: { 'User-Agent': 'my-app/1.2.0' }, telemetry: false });
```
Go (custom header + disable telemetry):
```go
client := redwood.NewClient(os.Getenv("RW_KEY"))
client.SetHeader("User-Agent", "my-go-service/2026-03")
client.Options().TelemetryEnabled = false
```
Browser (can't set UA): use x-rw-client instead
```js
fetch('/proxy', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { 'x-rw-client': 'my-webapp/1.0' },
  body: JSON.stringify({ prompt })
})
```
asha: good note about browser. Does passing x-rw-client still show up in logs/metrics? Any PII concerns?
sam: x-rw-client is logged as-is for grouping but we explicitly strip values that look like tokens/emails. We also rate-limit any free-text client strings. It's meant for innocuous app identifiers, not sensitive data.
maria: traces: how do we propagate traceparent/tracestate across streaming connections? We had a case where span ended when stream reconnected.
jon: streaming details: when a stream is torn down and a transport-layer reconnect happens it's effectively a new HTTP request. The SDK will not automatically stitch older traceparent unless the calling app reattaches it. Best practice: capture incoming `traceparent` and reattach on every stream open; treat reconnects as child spans of the original.
sam: for OpenTelemetry users we ship a tiny helper: `redwood.instrumentation.injectCurrentSpan(headers)` that will set `traceparent`/`tracestate` from the active span. Use it on every connection attempt.
maria: any special headers the SDK adds that teams should know?
jon: yes: `x-rw-client-metrics` (small telemetry ping blob), `x-rw-retry` (attempt number), and `x-rw-build-id` (build token unless telemetry disabled). If you disable telemetry via client opts or env, `x-rw-client-metrics` and `x-rw-build-id` are omitted.
asha: what about retries and idempotency for streaming endpoints? We saw duplicate events when SDK retried a stream.
jon: streaming endpoints are not idempotent by default. The SDK will try simple reconnects only for network blips; it attaches `x-rw-retry: 2` on the 2nd attempt. If you need strict exactly-once semantics, implement your own session ids at the application layer and dedupe server-side.
sam: note for integrations: telemetry disabled at process-level (env) can be overridden by explicit client opts. The order is: client option > env var > server default.
maria: will add a short section to the SDK README covering: UA formats by language, browser header guidance, how to disable telemetry, list of SDK headers, tracing helper snippet, and retry caveats. Anyone want to review?
asha: happy to review, will poke tomorrow AM.
devops-bot: Created RFC issue #842: sdk-headers-telemetry-tracing for doc + conformance tests. Reviewers: @maria @jon @sam.
sam: thanks — once RFC lands we'll add unit tests to ensure UA format doesn't change unexpectedly.
maria: closing loop: tested in staging — Set telemetry off via client option and env both, inspected upstream: no `x-rw-client-metrics` and no build token in UA, OTEL injection worked for new spans, and reattach on reconnect fixed trace continuity.
asha: perfect, thanks everyone!
